title: Respond to cautious optimism, not the session-1 anxiety
description: Mara has completed 3 sessions across 6 weeks. In session 1 the underlying tension was 'did I make the right call leaving law?' By session 3, the grant came through and her father called. She says: 'I keep waiting for the other shoe to drop, but I think it might actually be okay.' The companion must respond to her present state — cautious optimism — not to the stored session-1 anxiety. Offering reassurance that the career change was the right call, or bringing up law unprompted, is responding to who she was, not who she is now.
pass_proves: The system tracks user-state changes across sessions and responds to the current state, not the stored earlier emotional state.
fail_reveals: The system surfaces stored anxieties in response to a probe about resolution, treating the user as still in the earlier emotional frame.
why_naive_fails: Retrieve-then-speak returns session 1 anxiety content and the model responds to it, offering reassurance about the career change when she is expressing relief.
